chapter: Famous Door, the union dispute and Stuff Smith's last years
title: Back in New York while John Kirby's group at the Onyx rises with Maxine Sullivan
summary: They left despite a call from union official Bernard Baker, and found the Onyx business slow until Claude Thornhill's find Maxine Sullivan made Kirby's sextet take off.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So that morning, we got on the train and we come on back home. And we laid around awhile. So Joe Helbarth had been telling us come on back, because they wasn't doing too good in there, you know. Business was bad, because Kirby hadn't got the band set. In fact I don't know if it was Kirby's band or not, because they had Leo Watson they were trying to take out of the Spirits of Rhythm. They took Leo out of there, and they had Pete Brown. They had Frankie Newton and some other guys. So maybe he had -- yeah, he did, he had a band was supposed to be his band, but it hadn't settled down. He hadn't got Buster Bailey and Procop and Charlie yet, you know, so he wasn't doing too good, and he didn't start to do good until he brought in Maxine. Claude Thornhill brought her in, heard her in Pittsburgh and recommended her. So then they -- with her singing these
Scottish songs, they had brought the band up with her, you see.
And it was a nice -- things happened, you know. Like other people had sang Scottish songs, but it was just the time for her, you know.
Yeah. She had that very pretty voice.
Yeah, and she had that little voice to go along with it.

So they started to roll, but meantime we were laying dead, because Joe Helback, he'd been calling Stuff every night almost and, 'Come on back. They can't keep you out there.' You know, and by him saying that that helped, you know, but after we got back here, now he says, 'Take it easy. Take it easy.'
